Format: FADEBABE magic, BE, 16-byte header (capacity=4000 slots, live=971), 24-byte TOC entries sorted by hash, 2KB sector-aligned blocks. 972 live entries (header undercounts by 1). 521/972 are text (122 explicit CallScript fragments + 399 mixed text); 449 are binary blobs in 28 type categories (0x0A-0x29). Notably contains plain-text CallScript source code with syntax: ?i(cond){...}, #var, $#var, $Cnn opcodes, #mapid, #EventFlag, #ONESELF, etc. Found 1 nested FADEBABE archive (sub-manifest, 856 bytes).

156 unique $Cxx opcodes (range 0x01-0xBF), 1554+ #vars, 428 $#charvars, only ?i keyword. Most common: $CAC (2835x), $C05 (1241x), $C0D, $C28. Top vars: #taskid(17168x), #DDD/EEE/CCC/FFF (15k each). Position vars #MapX/Y/Z, #GoalX/Y/Z. Boot script manifest at 0x00203BB0: main.sol, walker.sol, walkerfunc.sol, mapoutend.sol, playerpos.sol. Scripts stored as .sol files in VOLUME.DAT.

Code region 0x16C000-0x180000 contains the script engine. Three VM main loops at 0x001654A0/0x00165B70/0x00165F70 (1020 bytes each, near-identical — likely for 3 parallel script contexts). If-statement evaluator at 0x0016DA00 (3940 bytes, refs ?i: error msgs). CScript container ctor at 0x0017FED0 (1252 bytes — sets up doubly-linked-list node with type tag 0x00223C68). Container ops at 0x1503c0/0x150d30 (likely std::map insert/find).

Did NOT find a contiguous jump table of 156 function pointers. The engine likely uses a switch cascade or hash-keyed lookup. Strong candidate region: 0x16C000-0x180000 contains 1860-byte FUN_0016cf00 + 3940-byte i_0016da00. Recommend opening these in Ghidra GUI for decompiler view to extract opcode->handler map. Tried scanning for sequential uint32 arrays in text-range — gave 773 false-positives (most were string-pointer tables).

LAYOUT: MDSP magic@base; +0x04 kmd_anim_ptr; pointer table 0x08..0x150 (u32 block-rel offsets, 0xFFFFFFFF=null) -> sub-blocks by magic: KMDp(mesh)/KMDs(skeleton)/TEXx(textures)/bone-table(no magic). KMDp: +0x04 vcount,+0x08 pcount,+0x10 vif_tag,+0x34 batch_size(40),+0x3C tex_id; body@+0x40 = interleaved [<=40 verts x32B][strip section]; inter-batch 16B hdr FFFFFFFF|bs|bs+1|tex. VERTEX 32B: +0x00 pos xyz f32, +0x0C bone_id u32 (SMALL INT = per-vertex rigid bone!), +0x10 normal xyz f32, +0x1C 0.0. STRIP sec: [VIFcode u32 cmd|num|imm][implicit UV u16u,u16v /4096][8B records: u16 raw_index(stride2 actual=raw/2), byte+3 strip_flag(0x80=restart), u16u,u16v UV /4096]. TEXx: +4 count + count u32 tex offsets. WHY MATTERS: writer only needs to emit KMDp submeshes; can REUSE Tesshu KMDs skeleton+bone-table+TEXx and swap only mesh. topic: ROOT CAUSE of the frame freeze: gzmfs READ overwrites the loaded code image
details:
boot_p7j2.log.err line 33630 -- the first bad dispatch is immediately preceded by:
  [gzmfs] READ fd=0 pos=93194240 len=527456 -> 527456 dst=0x0021D808
  [dispatch:first-bad-pc] bad=0x4f4f1225 ra=0x13a474 sp=0xfbfc0 v0=0x4f4f1225 a0=0x2 a1=0x8000 trace=0x10ecc0 -> 0x10ec90 -> 0x11c320
dst=0x21D808 + len=527456 spans 0x21D808..0x29E2E8. The ELF PT_LOAD (code+rodata) is 0x100000..0x224880, so this read writes OVER the running program image, including the jump table at 0x222520 and 0x223450 (the nearestStart in the dispatcher warning). bad==v0 means the branch target came from $v0, i.e. a jalr through a pointer loaded from the clobbered table; 0x4f4f1225 is file payload, not code. 3966 identical bad dispatches follow, which is the FRAMES_FROZEN symptom (idx pinned at 4730 while dma/gif keep climbing and [p4:vbl] keeps ticking to 20100 -- vblank is healthy, the guest is stuck retrying a garbage indirect call).
This ALSO explains the long-standing 0x55282233 stomp at 0x222520 (finding 182 class): same mechanism, different file bytes. The residual corruptor is NOT a heap free-list bug -- it is a file read landing on the code image.
OPEN QUESTION: is dst=0x21D808 a corrupt pointer, or a legitimate static buffer whose read length is wrong? Next: log the caller ra for any gzmfs read whose [dst,dst+len) intersects 0x100000..0x224880.

topic: CORRECTION to finding 191: the gzmfs code-overlap is probably BENIGN
details:
Finding 191 claimed the gzmfs READ to 0x21D808 was overwriting live code and therefore caused the bad-PC wedge. That overstated the evidence. Two facts against it:
1) All 7 "functions" in the written range (0x222b20..0x223330) are auto_named=1 with evidence=NULL, i.e. Ghidra auto-analysis guesses, not confirmed code (contrast: entry @0x100008 is CONFIRMED_GHIDRA). The region is most likely a static load buffer at the tail of the image.
2) The very next drive produced the SAME overlap 24x (dst=0x0021D808 len=527456 client=0x00C2D7C0 ra=0x001B5B60, caller hot_fx_001b5a60+0x100) with a VALID client pointer and ZERO bad dispatches, and the verdict improved to FRAMES_ADVANCING. Same overlap, no wedge => the overlap is correlation, not established causation.
The read destination is stable and the client is valid, so this is a deliberate load, not a corrupt pointer. Treat 0x21D808 as a legitimate buffer unless a confirmed symbol is found in the range.

topic: STRATEGIC: CPU translation is not the blocker - the GS raster path is
details:
Measured, not assumed:
* Function coverage: 2820 functions cover 989,512 of the 1,198,208-byte PT_LOAD (82.6%). Of the 192,364 uncovered bytes, capstone decodes only 9,784 bytes (62 gaps) as >92% valid MIPS; the largest gap (147,460 B @0x1feb1c) decodes 6.3% and is plainly data. So the recompiler translated essentially all the code - missing translation is NOT the blocker.
* Symbol quality: 2819/2820 are auto_named=1; only 70 carry CONFIRMED_GHIDRA. A broader Ghidra rescan adds nothing - the auto-analysis ceiling is already hit. Only targeted manual RE of specific functions is worth doing.
* 0x151910 is NOT a wedge: it decodes to lw/addiu/sw of a counter at 0x1C($s3) around jal func_133D00 - a main-loop iteration counter. The debugger panel even states its snapshot is best-effort while the guest runs. Combined with +2803 frames, the game IS executing its main loop.
* The actual visual blocker: the window shows a FLAT CLEAR COLOUR (mint green RGB 71,253,150; previously magenta) with nothing drawn over it, while dma climbs to 1.37M and gif to 19130. The framebuffer is cleared and presented every frame but primitives/textures produce no pixels. gsw (GS register writes) = 0.
CONCLUSION: remaining work is the machine around the CPU (GS raster + GIF image upload path), not the CPU translation. ps2_vu1.cpp and ps2_vif1_interpreter.cpp exist, so VU1 is stubbed/implemented and is a 3D-stage concern, not a title-screen one (vif=20 total, i.e. the geometry path is idle - correct for a 2D menu).

We own a golden reference that renders this title correctly; drive both to the same point and diff GS state (DISPFB, TEX0/CLUT, the GIF display list) instead of reasoning about our port in isolation.

topic: DISPROVED (my own hypothesis): texture uploads DO reach GS VRAM
details:
I suspected no texture upload was happening because grepping the logs for TRXDIR/BITBLTBUF returned 0. That was invalid: those identifiers appear only as case labels in ps2_gs_gpu.cpp and were never printed, so the count could only ever be 0. Added real telemetry [p4:gs-trx] at GS_REG_TRXDIR. Result, first 80s of boot:
  #1 dir=0 dst=0x0      dbw=8 dpsm=0x2C rrw=512 rrh=512 (262144 px)
  #7 dir=0 dst=0x69000  dbw=4 dpsm=0x00 rrw=256 rrh=128 (32768 px)
  #2,3,5,6 dir=0 dst=0xED000/40/80/C0 rrw=8 rrh=2 (16 px each) -> CLUTs
  #8 dir=0 dst=0xED100 rrw=16 rrh=16
dir=0 is host->local, the correct upload direction. So: uploads happen, TEX0 is written 96x, and 96 prim=6 (SPRITE) kicks occur - yet the window shows only a flat clear colour. The defect is therefore DOWNSTREAM of upload: rasterisation, texture sampling, or the draw target. Next instrument: for the first N sprite kicks log FRAME (fbp/fbw/psm), SCISSOR, TEST (ate/atst/zte), TEX0 (tbp/tbw/psm/cbp) and the two vertex coords, plus a count of pixels actually written, to see whether the sprites are rejected, drawn offscreen, or drawn into a buffer that is never displayed.

topic: ROOT NARROWED: rasterizer writes only 2559 black pixels the whole boot
details:
[p4:px] telemetry at the WriteVram store in GSRasterizer::writePixel. Whole boot (80s): only 2,559 pixel writes total. A single 640x224 frame is 143,360 pixels, so the rasterizer draws essentially NOTHING - the title art bulk is never rasterized. Every written pixel is pixel=0x80000000 = RGB(0,0,0) A=0x80 (solid black), to fbp_block=0x0 fbw=10 psm=0x1 (CT24), which is the DISPLAYED buffer (DISPFB fbp field=0). So the pixels that DO get written go to the right place but are black.
This overturns the framing: the flat clear colour is not being overdrawn because the game's imagery never reaches the rasterizer, not because it is drawn then hidden. Two sub-questions:
1) The 96 TEXTURED (tme=1) sprite kicks that follow the TEX0 writes: do they reach drawSprite, and does sampleTexture return transparent/zero so nothing is written? If textured sprites are the background/title art, a broken sampler or CLUT lookup would explain both the low write count and the flat screen.
2) The untextured sprites that DO write are black (vertex colour 0,0,0). Is the RGBAQ vertex colour being read at all, or defaulting to 0?
NEXT: log, per sprite, tme and the pixel count it produced; and for tme=1 log the first sampled texel. That isolates textured-vs-untextured and sampler-returns-zero from vertex-colour-is-zero.

topic: ROOT CAUSE of the black title: PSMT8 CLUT sampler returns opaque black
details:
Differential-strategy probe (per-sprite [p4:spx] + per-texel [p4:texel]) resolved the fork in ONE build. The title art is 8-bit CLUT-indexed (tpsm=0x13 = PSMT8), all from texture tbp=0x1A40. For all 16 sampled texels the sampler returns texel=0x80000000 = RGB(0,0,0) A=0x80 (opaque black), combined RGBA=00000080. 479/514 sprite kicks are tme=1 (textured); every one samples black. The rasterizer, coords, scissor, test, present buffer are all correct (proven earlier) - the INPUT is black because the CLUT lookup for PSMT8 yields black for every index.
This is the disease, not a symptom. Candidates within sampleTexture/lookupCLUT for PSMT8: (a) the 8-bit index read returns 0 (wrong texel-address swizzle for PSMT8), (b) the CLUT was never loaded to the address the sampler reads, or (c) the CLUT index / CBP / CSA computation is wrong so every lookup hits a black entry. Note [p4:gs-trx] earlier logged CLUT uploads of rrw=8 rrh=2 (16-entry) - those are PSMT4 (16-colour) CLUTs; a PSMT8 texture needs a 256-entry CLUT, which must be uploaded/located separately. Prime suspect: the 256-entry CLUT for PSMT8 is not where lookupCLUT reads it, or the sampler treats PSMT8 like a direct-colour format and reads RGB from an index buffer.
The untextured full-screen sprites (tme=0, 640x224, vtxRGBA=00000080) are a separate black BACKGROUND fill; secondary to the textured-art failure.
NEXT: read lookupCLUT + the PSMT8 branch of sampleTexture; log the raw 8-bit index and the CBP/CSA/CLUT address it reads, and compare against the CLUT upload destination from [p4:gs-trx].

topic: ROOT CAUSE PINNED: ReadVram(PSMT8) returns all-zero indices for the title texture
details:
[p4:clut] is decisive. For the PSMT8 title texture (tbp0=0x1A40 tbw=8) the raw 8-bit index is 0x00 at EVERY sampled (u,v) - 24/24 samples, u=0..5 v=0..1. The CLUT is fine: cbp=0x3B44 stable, and CLUT[0]=0 (black) is the normal transparent entry, so lookupCLUT returning 0x80000000 is correct FOR index 0. The bug is upstream of the CLUT: gs->ReadVram(GS_PSM_T8, tbp0=0x1A40, tbw=8, u, v) reads 0 across the whole texture.
So it is NOT the CLUT, NOT the vertex colour, NOT the rasterizer, NOT the coords/scissor/test/present (all previously proven correct). It is the 8-bit texel FETCH. Two candidates, both in the GS memory layer:
  (a) the PSMT8 texture data was never written to block 0x1A40 (the TRXDIR       upload landed elsewhere / different block-address units), or
  (b) ReadVram's PSMT8 address/swizzle disagrees with the write path's, so       reads miss the uploaded data. PS2 PSMT8 is stored swizzled; upload and       sample MUST use the same swizzle.
NEXT: read GS::ReadVram and the upload/processImageData PSMT8 paths in ps2_gs_memory.cpp / ps2_gs_gpu.cpp; log the upload dbp in BLOCK units + psm to confirm whether block 0x1A40 ever receives data; if it does, the swizzle pair is inconsistent. This is a single fixable function pair.

topic: SMOKING GUN: title texture uploaded as PSMCT32, read as PSMT8 - swizzle mismatch
details:
The complete mechanism, proven by cross-referencing [p4:clut] (read side) with [p4:gs-trx] (upload side) in the same boot:
READ side: sampler wants PSMT8 (tex.psm=0x13) at tbp0=0x1A40 tbw=8; every raw index reads 0x00.
UPLOAD side: my gs-trx prints dst=dbp*64, so block 0x1A40 == dst 0x69000. Upload #7 is exactly dst=0x69000 dbw=4 dpsm=0x0 (PSMCT32) rrw=256 rrh=128.
So the game UPLOADS the texture as PSMCT32 256x128 but READS it as PSMT8 with tbw=8 (512 wide). BYTE-COUNT PROOF this is intentional, not a bug in the game: 256*128*4 = 131072 bytes = exactly 512*256 PSMT8 indices. This is the standard PS2 idiom of uploading an 8-bit (or 4-bit) texture through a 32-bit BITBLT for DMA speed; the GS unswizzles on sample.
THE HLE BUG: WriteCT32 (upload path) and ReadP8 (sample path) do NOT lay the bytes out at consistent addresses, so ReadP8 at block 0x1A40 misses the data WriteCT32 wrote and returns 0. On hardware/PCSX2 the block+column swizzle is defined so a CT32 word and the four T8 texels occupying it map correctly; our two swizzle functions are inconsistent for the cross-format case.
FIX (needs verification against PCSX2 via the differential harness / a VRAM dump): make ReadP8/ReadP4 address the same physical bytes that WriteCT32 wrote for a given block, i.e. implement the PS2 PSMT8<->PSMCT32 (and PSMT4<->PSMCT32) block-swizzle equivalence, as PCSX2 does with its psm block/column tables. This is the LAST thing between the port and a visible title screen.
